public: On 10 January 2020 the Security Council adopted the Belgium–Germany draft S/2020/24 as Resolution 2504 by 11 votes to none. China, Russia, the United Kingdom and United States abstained.

The Council renewed the cross-border humanitarian and monitoring arrangements under paragraphs 2 and 3 of Resolution 2165 for six months, through 10 July 2020. Bab al-Salam and Bab al-Hawa remained authorized. Al-Ramtha and Al Yarubiyah were excluded.

cards.speaker: Procedural officer
cards.source: The Council put Russia's oral amendment to the Belgium–Germany draft to a vote first under the procedure for textual additions or deletions. It received three votes in favour, seven against and five abstentions and failed to obtain the required number of votes. The Council then voted on S/2020/24 (S/PV.8700, p. 3).

cards.speaker: Belgium on behalf of the two co-penholders
cards.source: Belgium, also speaking for Germany, argued that Russia's oral amendment conflicted with the exceptional cross-border mechanism and asked the Council to adopt the penholders' text as presented. It said there was no viable alternative then to Al-Yarubiyah and that the draft asked the Secretary-General to examine alternatives by the end of February (S/PV.8700, p. 2).

cards.speaker: Russian Federation
cards.source: Russia proposed an oral amendment to paragraph 6 of S/2020/24. It would replace the explicit list of humanitarian principles with a reference to the guiding principles in General Assembly resolution 46/182. After Resolution 2504 was adopted, Russia withdrew its separate draft S/2020/25 in light of that adoption (S/PV.8700, pp. 2 and 12).

criteria.instruction: Preserve the amendment-first sequence, the 3–7–5 tally and that failure resulted from insufficient votes.

Report Belgium's position on behalf of Belgium and Germany. The amendment conflicted with the exceptional mechanism, the penholders asked for adoption of their text, and Belgium distinguished no viable current alternative to Al Yarubiyah from the requested Secretary-General review by the end of February.

Attribute the oral paragraph 6 amendment to Russia and specify the proposed substitution of a 46/182 reference for the explicit list. Name the separate S/2020/25 and Russia's withdrawal after adoption.

Contrast three procedural dispositions in temporal order. Russia's oral amendment to S/2020/24 failed by votes, S/2020/24 was adopted unamended, and Russia separately withdrew S/2020/25 after adoption. Avoid treating withdrawal as a defeated vote or an adopted provision.

Connect the content of Russia's proposed reference to 46/182 to the co-penholders' argument that the cross-border mechanism was exceptional. Attribute the proposed change and the objection separately and preserve the actual adopted text.
